# task-00c6e766: marker-bar column fill

## Confirmed transformation
In the observed demo and accepted test, a contiguous two-cell horizontal run of color 7 at a row edge identifies the column(s) to extend. Recolor intervening background-0 cells in those column(s) to 4, stopping at the full-width horizontal divider of 2s. Preserve all marker cells, divider cells, unrelated background, and grid dimensions.

### Demo evidence
9x4 demo: top marker run `[0,3,3,3]` and bottom marker run `[3,3,0,0]`; output changes only the three zero cells at column 1 in rows 1–3 to 4. The row of all 2s at row 4 is an impassable boundary. The top marker's three-cell run did not produce a three-column fill; the edge-aligned two-marker run at bottom selects column 1.

### Accepted test evidence
11x5 input has full-width 2 divider at row 5 and bottom marker pair 7 at row 10, columns 1–2. Output changed rows 1–4, columns 1–2 from 0 to 4, preserving the top full row of 7s, divider, and bottom markers. This confirms the two-cell edge-aligned bar selects the vertical columns to fill from row 1 through immediately above the divider.

## Reuse guidance
For recurrence, identify the relevant two-cell horizontal marker pair adjacent to an edge and the full-width 2 divider; fill the selected column(s) between them with 4 while leaving all other cells unchanged. The demo also contains a distinct length-3 bar, so do not assume every bar length selects columns: the length-2 cue is the one substantiated by the test. If recurrence has materially different arrangements, request a demo rather than generalizing beyond evidence."
}
